How we work out the reputation
Each figure comes only from the freelancer\'s own work on Dorr, and none shows before there are at least 3 pieces of data behind it.
The clients\' score for quality, out of 5, turned into a figure out of 100. It needs at least 3 published ratings.

The share of approved parts delivered within their days. Days added by a change the client accepted count, and a part only starts once the client funds it, so late funding never counts against the freelancer.
The clients\' score for communication, out of 5, turned into a figure out of 100.

Of the projects that ended, the share that were finished. An end that was the client\'s fault, or nobody\'s, is left out; only an end that was the freelancer\'s responsibility counts against them. A project still running, or a dispute not yet decided, never counts.
Of the clients they finished a project for, the share who came back for another one.
From the levels of their best 3 certified skills (beginner 40, intermediate 60, advanced 80, expert 100), with their verified works shown beside it.
The overall score is the average of the known figures, and shows once at least 3 of them are known.
Excellent 85+ · Good 70+ · Fair 50+ · below that, needs work.
If one project makes a figure wrong, the freelancer can ask the Dorr team to review it; an accepted request takes that project out.
This work was done for a client on Dorr, and the client allowed it to be shown.
